content.comment_body: Hello everyone! I'm planning to purchase a [product_name] to set up an irrigation system for a village or farm. There is no wired internet available—only a portable WiFi router with a SIM card, which lacks an Ethernet (RJ45) port. I want to control the zones and valves remotely via my phone, using the webserver HMI function from home, which is about 50 km away. What equipment would I need to make internet access possible for the [product_name]? Should I consider a different router or modem? Any advice is welcome! Thanks in advance!​

You can use a WiFi repeater in Client mode so that the received WiFi signal is provided to the LAN output. Connect this LAN output to the [product_name]. Alternatively, you could get a standard router that offers LAN ports and a SIM-based fallback, which would replace your current portable WiFi router. For example, the TP-Link MR600 works fine here with a SIM card, providing both WiFi and LAN output. [url]

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users are discussing solutions for remotely controlling a [product_name] using mobile internet and WiFi, since there is no ethernet or wired internet available. The main challenge is enabling remote HMI access in a location with limited connectivity, and finding compatible hardware to bridge the [product_name] to the internet.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes to easily connect the [product_name] to the internet through WiFi and access it remotely by phone, utilizing webserver HMI functions from their home.
